summary: v1 - initial model: season Pythagorean expectation + log5 head-to-head + a flat +4pt home-field boost.
why: Baseline sabermetric approach - simple, well-established, and verifiable before adding anything fancier.

summary: v2 - added starter FIP + bullpen ERA + park factors; probability now projects game-specific runs instead of using season totals only. Also added line-movement tracking and the prediction-logging/backtesting infrastructure.
why: Season-aggregate alone ignores who's actually pitching today - the single biggest known blind spot. Also needed a way to check whether the model's stated probabilities are actually calibrated, not just plausible.

summary: v3 - reworked the odds display: real sportsbook moneyline next to the model's fair (no-vig) price, collapsed the mirrored home/away edge into one 'Model likes' column, added projected run differential.
why: The old win%-only display read like two separate findings instead of one and was confusing to scan.

summary: v4 - added compute_track_record(): win/loss record for resolved picks, bucketed by how big the edge was (10+ / 5-10 / 0-5 pts).
why: Needed a way to see whether the model's biggest disagreements with the market are actually the more reliable ones, not just louder.

summary: v5 - added per-game 'Why this prediction?' write-up, and started fetching each team's last-10 record / streak (recent form) for that write-up.
why: Raw numbers alone don't explain themselves - wanted the reasoning spelled out in plain sentences. Recent form was pulled in for the prose but was never wired into the probability calculation itself.

summary: v6/v7 - two visual redesign passes (design-system palette pass, then the 'ledger under the lights' box-score aesthetic).
why: Cosmetic only - no change to model math or picks.

summary: v8 - extended prediction logging to capture starter FIP, bullpen ERA, park factor, projected runs, recent form, and a model-version tag per pick. Added this Analysis tab: changelog, pick-by-pick postmortems (why a pick missed, or whether it was just normal variance), pattern detection, and a running list of accuracy-improvement ideas.
why: First day's reconciled record (1-4) included a 19-point model/market gap (Cubs @ Cardinals game) that turned out to be undiagnosable after the fact - report.json wasn't persisted and predictions_log.jsonl only kept the bare probabilities, not the inputs that produced them. This closes that gap going forward.

summary: v9 - reconciled the second day (2026-07-28): 20 graded picks combined, 8-12 (40%) overall, Brier score 0.2542 (slightly worse than a coin flip's 0.25 - not yet demonstrating real calibration). Generalized detect_patterns() to flag any CONFIDENCE_TIERS bucket that's meaningfully below breakeven at n>=8 (currently: Low-confidence/0-5pt picks are 3-8, 27%).
why: A first look at edge in narrow custom bands seemed to show a stark '3-5pt edge = 0-for-5' pattern, but that used bin boundaries chosen after seeing the data - re-checked with neutral, uniform-width bins and the effect mostly vanished into small-sample noise. Recorded here as a caution against boundary-shopping, and to explain why the pattern check below uses the pre-existing tier boundaries instead of custom bands.

summary: v10 - blended recent form (last-10 record) into adjusted_win_probability() as a small, capped nudge (model.RECENT_FORM_WEIGHT = 0.06, max +/-6 points at the extreme of a 10-0 team facing a 0-10 team). Season offense/pitching/park still does nearly all of the work.
why: Justified independent of the 20-game backtest, unlike a weight retune would be: mlb_data.get_team_recent_form() was already being fetched for every game and thrown away except in the prose write-up. Deliberately NOT a response to the Low-confidence-tier weakness flagged in v9 - that would be tuning to noise. Whether this actually improves accuracy needs a fresh batch of resolved picks made under this version to tell.

summary: v11 - added client-side live score polling: the page now fetches MLB's public schedule endpoint directly from the browser every ~90s (paused when the tab isn't visible, stops entirely once every game today is Final) and updates each game's score/Live-Final pill in place - no rebuild, no commit, no deploy involved.
why: GitHub's Actions `schedule:` trigger turned out to fire every 1.5-3 hours in practice rather than the configured 30 minutes (a platform limitation, not a bug here), so scores on the site were up to ~an hour stale. Rather than force more frequent commits/deploys (which would also make the git history noisier), scores now update live in the visitor's browser while predictions/edges keep updating on the existing, unchanged, infrequent rebuild cadence - the two don't need the same freshness, so they no longer share one.

summary: v12 - UI fix: 'Model likes' and 'Proj. run diff' (plus 'Line move' and 'Books') had no visible column label on desktop at all - they used a .mobile-label class that only turns on below 780px, while 'Book'/'Model' used a separate always-visible .price-label class. Unified all six columns onto the one that actually shows. Also found the game-card grid had gap:0 with padding-right zeroed out on every numeric column, meaning zero gutter between them; added a real grid gap instead.
why: Flagged directly by Matt ("labels ... are missing", "spacing is a little off"). Confirmed both by reading the CSS rather than guessing, and cross-checked the fix against the ui-ux-pro-max skill's visible-label and spacing-consistency guidance before shipping.

summary: Ops fix (not a model/UI version bump): the workflow's git push had no retry logic, so any two runs overlapping even briefly (a manual trigger landing seconds before/after a scheduled one) caused the second to fail outright with a rejected non-fast-forward push - losing that cycle's data update. Added a fetch+rebase+retry loop around the push.
why: Hit this for real: a manual dispatch and the schedule trigger landed 19 seconds apart, and the second run failed clean rather than silently - good that it was loud, but it shouldn't have needed a human to notice and re-run it. report.json/predictions_log.jsonl/odds_history.jsonl are machine-regenerated each run (never hand-edited), so rebasing onto whatever the other run just pushed is always safe here.

summary: v13 - fixed a real bug: a finished game (Marlins, 2026-07-29) showed 'not a graded pick' even though it WAS logged with a real 8.4pt edge earlier that day - the Odds API stops returning lines for finished games, so a fresh report.json rebuild loses home_edge/away_edge for any game that's since gone Final. dashboard._final_result_str() now falls back to the logged pick (predictions_log.jsonl) when the live report has none. Also implemented the two remaining open FUTURE_ADJUSTMENTS: outsized edges (>=15pt, dashboard.OUTLIER_EDGE_PTS) now get a visible warning flag on the live pick itself, and backtest.compute_home_away_split() is now always computed and shown on the Analysis tab, with detect_patterns() flagging a >=25-point home-vs-away gap once both sides have 8+ picks.
why: Matt flagged the Marlins bug directly. The other two were the last unimplemented items on the improvement-ideas list from v9 - both are presentation/observability additions (no model math changed), so they don't carry the same overfitting risk as a weight change would.

summary: v14 - full code review pass looking for real bugs (not weight tuning). Found and fixed one with real accuracy impact: pitching.get_pitcher_season_stats()/get_recent_starts() crashed with IndexError when the API returned an empty (not absent) stats list - which happens for any pitcher with no season data logged yet (e.g. a rookie's MLB debut). Because that crash was caught by one broad try/except covering BOTH starters' entire pitching/bullpen/park block, one pitcher having no data silently degraded the WHOLE game - both teams - down to season-only Pythagorean, discarding the other team's perfectly good starter/bullpen/park data too. Fixed to fail isolated per-pitcher instead. Also surfaced the existing (already-tracked but never displayed) pitching_error flag as a visible 'season-only' warning on the Model column, for the rarer cases it still fires.
why: This one has real, mechanical accuracy impact independent of any backtest sample size - a rookie call-up isn't rare over a season, and each occurrence was previously costing the model its best available data on the OTHER team too, not just the debuting pitcher's side.

summary: v15 - new NRFI (No Run First Inning) tab, a separate model (new nrfi.py) framed from three prompt templates saved in the vault (70-learning/sports-betting/001-nrfi-ai-prompt-templates.md): Inning Split (each starter's real first-inning-only stat split, MLB's official sitCodes=i01), Order Check (today's actual posted lineup - when available - top ~4 hitters' real season OBP), Rust Factor (real days since last start, capped nudge for short/long rest). Combined via a Poisson model of runs allowed in one inning. No fabricated inputs: verified the first-inning split is real per-pitcher data via a live query before building on it, and weather was left out entirely since no free source for it is wired in.
why: Matt asked to build a real model off that vault note, not just leave it as reference material. Known v1 gaps, stated plainly rather than glossed over: no market-line comparison yet (couldn't verify The Odds API's free tier even offers a first-inning market without a live key to test), and NRFI picks aren't logged/graded by backtest.py yet (needs a way to pull each game's actual 1st-inning score after the fact, not yet built) - so unlike the main model, there's no accuracy track record for this one yet.

summary: v16 - NRFI history and tracking (new nrfi_backtest.py, new nrfi_log.jsonl): every NRFI pick is logged with its full factor breakdown, then reconciled against the real 1st-inning score from MLB's linescore endpoint (nrfi.get_linescore_first_inning()) - notably, this resolves as soon as a game's 1st inning is over, not the whole game, so NRFI history builds up faster than the main model's. Track record and per-pick postmortems now show on the NRFI tab. Seeded the log with today's real picks: 16 logged, 10 already resolved (5-5, 90% observed NRFI rate - both numbers from a single day, not yet meaningful).
why: Matt asked for this directly, closing the gap flagged in v15. Wired into run_daily.py (reconcile before fetch, log after) and refresh.yml (nrfi_log.jsonl now persisted across runs, same as the other log files) so it runs unattended going forward, same as the main model's tracking.

summary: Data-integrity pass, prompted by Matt spotting the outlier warning flags on today's slate and asking why the record looked thin on high-confidence picks. Investigated both: (1) the two >=15pt outlier flags today (Nationals@Phillies 23.6pt, Dodgers@Cubs 18.0pt) are real model output, not a bug - Nationals@Phillies is driven by a real starter FIP gap (Alvarez 3.10 vs Nola 5.08) but Alvarez's FIP comes from only 7 starts, already self-flagged in the writeup as unstable; Dodgers@Cubs is a near-even game-specific run projection (4.41 vs 4.35, from two starters with almost identical FIP) where the +4pt home-field boost alone tips the model to Cubs, which mostly erases the two teams' real season-quality gap (+150 vs +89 run diff) that the market is pricing in - a real modeling limitation worth watching (matchup projections wash out season-strength gaps whenever the two starters happen to grade out close), not a fix. (2) Root-caused why 2026-07-27's record looks incomplete: 6 games that day (including the Marlins@Phillies game described in this README's own 'Verified live' section) were logged before the odds key was fully wired up, so they have no market_prob and can never be scored - by design, log_predictions() refuses to backfill a pick after a game has already resolved, since assigning one with the result already known would be grading with hindsight, not a real prediction. That gap is being left as-is rather than patched with reconstructed numbers. Did find and fix one real, unambiguous bug in the same area: reconcile() only ever checked each pick's ORIGINAL date for a Final result, so a postponed-and-resumed game (Braves@Mets, 2026-07-28, replayed 2026-07-29 under the same gamePk) stayed "unresolved" forever even after it was long since played - also tightened the Final-game filter to codedGameState=="F" rather than abstractGameState=="Final", since MLB's API marks a postponed game's own entry abstractGameState:"Final" too (codedGameState:"D" for discontinued), which the old check let through even though it never produced a usable result. Ran the fixed reconcile() once by hand: resolved 2 previously-stuck picks (both low/medium confidence, so this does not change the high-confidence tier).
why: Matt directly flagged the outlier warnings and asked whether the official history was missing high-confidence picks. Wanted a documented answer either way rather than silently patching numbers - the 07-27 gap is real but not safely fixable without fabricating a market read that was never actually captured; the postponed-game bug was safely fixable with live current data and is now fixed going forward.

summary: v18 - NRFI tab layout + tracking upgrade, both requested by Matt. (1) Added confidence tiers to nrfi_backtest.compute_track_record() (High/Medium/Low, bucketed by how far the model's own nrfi_prob leans from 50/50 - there's still no market line for NRFI, so this is lean-based rather than edge-vs-market like the main model). Thresholds (20/10pt) picked from the actual observed distribution of logged picks, and the tiers are computed fresh from the full nrfi_log.jsonl history every time, so they immediately reflect all picks already logged, not just new ones going forward. First real read: High-confidence (20+pt lean) picks are 9-14 (39%), actually WORSE than Low-confidence (0-10pt lean) picks at 19-8 (70%) - counter to what you'd want, and the reason this tier breakdown was worth building. Still early (23 High-tier picks total) but a real, unignorable signal once the sample grows. (2) Moved the resolved-picks history to the bottom of the NRFI tab (after today's picks, not before), and limited it to just the most recently resolved date - it was previously showing the entire history inline near the top, which only gets longer and pushes today's actual picks further down every single day.
why: Matt asked for both directly after noticing the NRFI history was cluttering the top of the tab, and asked separately whether we could narrow down which NRFI picks are actually worth trusting. The high-vs-low-confidence inversion found while building this is exactly the kind of thing this tier breakdown is meant to catch - noted here rather than acted on, since 23 High-tier picks is still too small a sample to retune anything from (same discipline as the main model - see the 2026-08-03 high-confidence-tier entry above).
